problems.q: Sold merchandise on account to Maple Supply for $4,000. Which special journal records this sale?
problems.why: The Sales Journal records sales of merchandise on account.

problems.q: Purchased merchandise on account from Summit Wholesale for $2,800. Which special journal records it?
problems.why: The Purchases Journal records merchandise bought on account.

problems.q: Received $3,000 cash from Bright Path Co. on its account. Where is it recorded?
problems.why: Any cash coming in goes in the Cash Receipts Journal.

problems.q: Paid Oakridge Supply $2,500 cash on account. Where is it recorded?
problems.why: Any cash going out goes in the Cash Payments Journal.

problems.q: Recorded the adjusting entry for supplies used during the year. Where does it go first?
problems.why: Adjusting entries are not routine, so they go in the General Journal.

problems.q: You need to see how much each customer owes. Which book do you check?
problems.why: The Accounts Receivable Subsidiary Ledger has one account per customer.

problems.q: You need to see how much the company owes each supplier. Which book do you check?
problems.why: The Accounts Payable Subsidiary Ledger has one account per supplier.

problems.q: Which book holds every account, with a running balance for each?
problems.why: The General Ledger is the book of all accounts and their balances.

problems.q: Which book of original entry records general entries in date order, as debits and credits?
problems.why: The General Journal is a book of original entry; the ledger comes after posting.

problems.q: Which record lists small payments made from the petty cash fund, one voucher at a time?
problems.why: The Petty Cash Record tracks each payment made from the fund.

problems.q: Which record shows units on hand and unit cost for each product, updated after every purchase and sale?
problems.why: Under the perpetual system, the Inventory Subsidiary Ledger tracks each product.

problems.q: Which record shows cost, useful life, and accumulated depreciation for each delivery truck?
problems.why: The Plant Asset Subsidiary Ledger keeps one card or account per long-term asset.

problems.q: Which listing shows every ledger balance to check that debits equal credits?
problems.why: A trial balance lists all account balances and compares total debits to credits.

problems.q: Which tool has columns for unadjusted balances, adjustments, and adjusted balances side by side?
problems.why: A worksheet lays out the adjusting process in columns before statements are prepared.

problems.q: Which document compares the bank statement with the company's Cash account?
problems.why: A bank reconciliation explains the difference between bank and book balances.

problems.q: Which record shows each employee's gross pay, withholdings, and net pay for a pay period?
problems.why: The Payroll Register summarizes pay and deductions for every employee.

problems.q: Sold merchandise to a customer for cash. Where is it recorded?
problems.why: The Sales Journal is only for credit sales, so a cash sale goes in the Cash Receipts Journal.

problems.q: Purchased office equipment on account from Clearwater Inc. Where is it recorded?
problems.why: The Purchases Journal is only for merchandise, so equipment goes in the General Journal.

problems.q: Maple Supply returned damaged merchandise for credit. Which journal records the return?
problems.why: A sales return is not a new sale, so it is recorded in the General Journal.

problems.q: Paid the monthly rent by check. Where is it recorded?
problems.why: All cash payments are recorded in the Cash Payments Journal.

problems.q: Sold an old computer for cash. Where is the cash received recorded?
problems.why: Any cash received goes in the Cash Receipts Journal, whatever its source.

problems.q: Recorded the closing entries at year-end. Where do they go first?
problems.why: Closing entries are journalized in the General Journal and then posted to the ledger.

problems.q: Individual credit sales are posted daily to which book?
problems.why: Each credit sale is posted to the customer's account in the Accounts Receivable Subsidiary Ledger.

problems.q: Individual credit purchases are posted daily to which book?
problems.why: Each credit purchase is posted to the supplier's account in the Accounts Payable Subsidiary Ledger.

problems.q: Which record supports the amount of the check written to replenish the petty cash fund?
problems.why: The Petty Cash Record totals what the fund paid out, which sets the check amount.

problems.q: The Accounts Receivable account in the General Ledger should equal the total of which book?
problems.why: The subsidiary ledger's account balances must add up to the control account.

problems.q: Found a service charge on the bank statement that the books do not show. Where do you list it?
problems.why: A bank reconciliation lists unrecorded bank charges so the books can be corrected.

problems.q: Which document ends with an adjusted bank balance and an adjusted book balance that should agree?
problems.why: A bank reconciliation brings the bank and book balances to the same correct amount.

problems.q: Paid a $45 postage bill from the petty cash fund. Where is the payment first recorded?
problems.why: Payments from the fund are first recorded in the Petty Cash Record.

problems.q: Wrote a check to reimburse the petty cash fund. Which book records the check?
problems.why: Writing a check is a cash payment, so it goes in the Cash Payments Journal.

problems.q: At month-end, which journal's column total is posted as Dr Accounts Receivable and Cr Sales Revenue?
problems.why: The Sales Journal total of credit sales is posted to the General Ledger at month-end.

problems.q: Which tool helps you organize amounts for the financial statements before adjusting and closing entries are posted?
problems.why: A worksheet collects balances and adjustments to build the statements.

problems.q: After closing entries are posted, which listing confirms debits still equal credits?
problems.why: A post-closing trial balance checks the ledger after closing.

problems.q: Issued new Common Stock for $5,000 cash. Where is it recorded?
problems.why: Cash received from selling stock goes in the Cash Receipts Journal.

problems.q: Paid a cash dividend to shareholders. Where is the payment recorded?
problems.why: Cash dividends paid go in the Cash Payments Journal.

problems.q: The board declared a dividend: Dr Dividends / Cr Dividends Payable. Where is it recorded?
problems.why: No cash moved yet, so the declaration goes in the General Journal.

problems.q: Recorded accrued salaries at year-end. Where is the entry first recorded?
problems.why: Accrual adjustments are entered in the General Journal.

problems.q: Where do you look for the running balance of the Cash account?
problems.why: A ledger account shows running balances; a journal does not.

problems.q: Returned damaged merchandise to Summit Wholesale for credit. Where is the purchase return recorded?
problems.why: A return is not a new purchase, so it goes in the General Journal.

problems.q: Received a $200 credit memo from Bluebird Traders for returned goods. Which subsidiary ledger is updated?
problems.why: The credit memo lowers what the company owes that supplier.

problems.q: Purchased merchandise from Oakridge Supply and paid cash on delivery. Where is it recorded?
problems.why: The Purchases Journal is only for credit purchases, so a cash purchase goes in the Cash Payments Journal.

problems.q: Wrote off an uncollectible customer account against the allowance. Where is the entry first recorded?
problems.why: No cash moved, and no special journal covers a write-off, so it goes in the General Journal.

problems.q: A customer wants 50 units of one product. Which record shows how many units are on hand?
problems.why: The Inventory Subsidiary Ledger tracks units in, out, and on hand for each product.

problems.q: At month-end, which journal's total is posted as Dr Merchandise Inventory and Cr Accounts Payable?
problems.why: The Purchases Journal total of credit purchases is posted to the General Ledger at month-end.

problems.q: The bank returned a customer's check marked NSF. Which document lists it as a correction to the book balance?
problems.why: An NSF check is a reconciling item that reduces the Cash balance in the books.

problems.q: Purchased supplies on account for office use. Where is it recorded?
problems.why: The Purchases Journal is only for merchandise, so supplies go in the General Journal.

problems.q: Which record's totals support the journal entry that records a payroll?
problems.why: The Payroll Register totals give the gross pay, withholdings, and net pay for the entry.

problems.q: Which book is the final destination of all posting from the journals?
problems.why: Journal amounts are posted to the General Ledger accounts.

problems.q: A delivery van is being sold. Which record shows its cost and depreciation so you can find the gain or loss?
problems.why: The Plant Asset Subsidiary Ledger holds cost and accumulated depreciation for each asset.

problems.q: Recorded a bank loan received in the checking account. Where is it recorded?
problems.why: Cash received from a loan goes in the Cash Receipts Journal.
